claims.head: The Blue Jackets hound the puck, the Blackhawks sit back
claims.body: On forecheck pressure, Columbus is one of the league’s best, but Chicago is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Expect the Blue Jackets to win more pucks back deep in the Blackhawks’ end.

CHI.head: The Blackhawks face a real test
CHI.body: Even though Chicago has home-ice advantage, Columbus has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Blackhawks can pull it off if their penalty kill holds up.

story.head: Somebody has to win
paras: The Blackhawks (5-13-1) beat Buffalo 3-2 in overtime on Nov 12, while the Blue Jackets are on a three-game losing streak. Both teams are near the bottom of the standings. Going in, the Blue Jackets are last in the Metropolitan (29th in the NHL) and the Hawks last in the Central (31st).

The Blue Jackets have played better than their record (.412) says: their chances are worth about .486, and their finishing has held them back. The Blackhawks haven’t played well, but their record (.289) is worse than their play: their chances are worth about .374, and their goaltending has held them back.

The Blue Jackets get their defensemen shooting (2nd) and get pinned in their own end on long shifts (29th). They also forecheck as hard as almost anyone (3rd), so the Blue Jackets hound the puck, but the Blackhawks sit back. Columbus has scored 2.35 goals a game, the third fewest in the league. On the other side, the Blackhawks pick their shots (lowest), have struggled on the power play (32nd) and don't block many shots (31st). Chicago has scored 2.21 goals a game, the fewest in the league, and allowed 4.11, the second most.

Kent Johnson (8 G / 9 A / 17 P in 17 GP) leads the Blue Jackets in scoring. Zach Werenski (2 G / 12 A / 14 P in 17 GP) isn’t far behind, with a point in six straight games against Chicago. For the Blackhawks, Connor Bedard (5 G / 10 A / 15 P in 13 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Roman Kantserov (9 G / 3 A / 12 P in 19 GP) has a team-high nine goals.

Spencer Knight (5-10-0 / .883 SV% in 15 GS) will likely start for Chicago. Columbus has two options in net: Jet Greaves (2-7-0 / .881 SV% in 9 GS) and Cam Talbot (5-3-0 / .907 SV% in 8 GS). They have split the last ten starts, and Greaves got the last one on Nov 12. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
